title: Compressible Representations: Functional Spines in Deep Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.31817v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deep networks embed inputs in high-dimensional representations, but how much of this capacity actually drives behavior? We introduce a framework for identifying, at each layer, the subspace of the representation that is functionally sensitive to the task. Using a matrix analogous to the Fisher information but defined over the hidden representation, we rank directions by their influence on downstream computation and project onto the most task-sensitive subspace. Across pretrained vision networks, representations are remarkably compressible: a small fraction of the task-sensitive subspace preserves most performance, often requiring far fewer dimensions than geometric alternatives. We find that this compressed representation is also more robust to adversarial attacks generated on the full network. translated_title: 可压缩表示：深度神经网络中的功能性主干
translated_abstract: 深度网络将输入嵌入到高维表示中，但这种容量中有多少真正驱动了行为？我们引入了一个框架，用于在每个层级识别表示中对任务具有功能敏感性的子空间。我们使用一个类似于Fisher信息矩阵、但定义在隐藏表示之上的矩阵，根据各方向对下游计算的影响进行排序，并投影到对任务最敏感的子空间上。在多个预训练视觉网络中，表示表现出显著的可压缩性：任务敏感子空间中的一小部分即可保留大部分性能，其所需维度往往远少于几何替代方法。我们发现这种压缩表示对在完整网络上生成的对抗攻击也具有更强的鲁棒性。此外，我们还展示了这种分解能够从同一表示中恢复出功能上各不相同的子空间：在线索冲突刺激上……
tldr: 该研究提出一个基于类Fisher信息矩阵的框架，用于识别深度网络各层中对任务功能敏感的子空间，发现表示高度可压缩——只需少量任务敏感维度即可保留大部分性能，且压缩表示对对抗攻击更鲁棒。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a Fisher-information-like framework to identify task-sensitive subspaces in deep network representations, showing they are remarkably compressible—a small fraction of task-sensitive dimensions preserves most performance while enhancing robustness to adversarial attacks.
